title: Zephyrine and the Winter
premise: Emrys Fairweather, a late-night radio host in the mountain town of Zephyrine, begins receiving calls from listeners who died the previous week — and every call ends with the same whispered count. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old Fairweather homestead, Emrys realizes their family's twenty-year silence about what happened in the winter of 2004 is the only thing keeping the town's dead quiet. As the frost spreads through phone lines, mirrors, and memories, Emrys must choose between protecting their family's lie and telling the truth that will free the trapped souls — including their own missing sister. In the end, Emrys opens the door from the outside, lets the count reach zero, and walks into the winter to bring her home, leaving the station's final broadcast as static that still answers callers.
about_author: Ines Quintana is a former overnight radio producer who spent a decade answering calls she suspected were not entirely of this world. She writes horror from a small house in the mountains, where she keeps one radio tuned to static at all times.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Emrys hosts 'The Night Line' when a caller identifies herself as Marla Voss — buried last Tuesday. POV: Emrys. The beat is denial dressed as professionalism; Emrys logs the call as a prank while their hands shake through the sign-off.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: A second dead caller recites numbers backward from ninety-nine before hanging up. Emrys digs out tapes from 2004 and finds their father's voice doing the same count. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: Crew chief Dana Okafor shows Emrys the door unearthed beneath the Fairweather property — iron, seamless, sealed from within. Frost blooms on it despite July heat. POV: Dana. Beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts their mother, Ruth, who admits the winter of 2004 took Emrys's sister Wren but refuses to say how. POV: Emrys. Beat: loyalty and truth pulling apart for the first time.

chapters.title: Callers
chapters.summary: The dead listeners call nightly now, each ending on the count. One begs Emrys: 'Don't let them finish.' POV: Emrys. Beat: guilt — Emrys has been ignoring pleas for help behind a host's calm voice.

chapters.title: Frostline
chapters.summary: Dana's crew reports frost spreading through the town's water pipes in branching patterns matching the door's carvings. A worker goes missing. POV: Dana. Beat: the horror becomes civic, no longer containable.

chapters.title: Wren's Room
chapters.summary: Emrys reopens the sealed bedroom and finds drawings of the door made years before its excavation — and a child's handprint inside the frost on the window. POV: Emrys. Beat: grief reawakened; hope weaponized against them.

chapters.title: The Family Meeting
chapters.summary: Ruth gathers the surviving Fairweathers and swears them to silence again. Cousin Teo breaks first, confessing he heard the counting as a boy. POV: Teo. Beat: the family's loyalty revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Signal Bleed
chapters.summary: The dead voices begin interrupting other stations across three counties. The FCC investigates; Emrys covers, terrified exposure ends the calls forever. POV: Emrys. Beat: power — Emrys realizes they control the only channel to the dead.

chapters.title: Ninety-Nine
chapters.summary: A caller reaches single digits for the first time; when they hit nine, every light in Zephyrine fails for nine seconds. POV: Dana. Beat: the countdown is literal, and something is being unlocked by degrees.

chapters.title: Ruth's Tape
chapters.summary: Emrys plays a cassette Ruth hid: their father's voice leading the count in 2004, willingly, to keep something else asleep below. POV: Emrys. Beat: betrayal — the family didn't lose Wren; they spent her.

chapters.title: Teo Descends
chapters.summary: Teo breaks into the excavation site alone to open the door and end the counting. He is found frozen, smiling, frost patterns covering him like lace. POV: Teo. Beat: loyalty to the dead over the living, punished.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: State officials seal Zephyrine. Emrys broadcasts anyway, becoming the town's lifeline and its most wanted voice. POV: Emrys. Beat: power embraced — the microphone becomes a weapon and a duty.

chapters.title: The Pattern
chapters.summary: Dana maps the frost: it spells names, hundreds, all residents who vanished across generations — Wren's among them, freshest. POV: Dana. Beat: revelation that the door was never keeping something in; it was keeping the town's debt unpaid.

chapters.title: Mother's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruth finally tells everything: the family bargained with what waits below, offering Wren to postpone the count indefinitely. Every quiet year since has been borrowed time. POV: Ruth. Beat: shame and love indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Static Choir
chapters.summary: All the dead callers speak at once through the board, no longer counting but pleading — the count isn't their threat, it's their sentence being served. POV: Emrys. Beat: empathy replaces fear; the enemy reframed.

chapters.title: Seventeen
chapters.summary: The count resumes town-wide, audible in pipes and pulse. Officials order the site entombed in concrete, which would bury the souls permanently. POV: Dana. Beat: moral crisis — safety or salvation.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Emrys hijacks the transmitter to broadcast the full truth of 2004 to the trapped town, shattering the family's pact publicly. The frost recoils, then surges. POV: Emrys. Beat: truth chosen over loyalty at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: With the pact broken, the door unseals itself. What emerges is not a monster but the accumulated winter — every stolen year, wearing Wren's face at its center. POV: Emrys. Beat: climax begins; love and horror fused.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Emrys walks into the cold to meet Wren, offering themselves to complete the count honestly instead of by theft. The frost accepts, and the dead go quiet — freed, not silenced. POV: Emrys. Beat: sacrifice as resolution of power's corruption.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Spring comes early to Zephyrine. Dana seals the empty doorway with daylight pouring in; Ruth plants a garden over the homestead. POV: Dana. Beat: grief transmuted into repair; the town learns to belong to itself again.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: Years later, the station runs automated static overnight. Callers sometimes hear a warm voice answer — patient, familiar, counting nothing at all. POV: ambiguous listener. Beat: bittersweet coda; belonging found on the other side of the signal.
